Posted July 13, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored Advanced Nutrients.

The Illinois Republican Party recently found itself without a candidate for the US Senate in the November elections when its nominee had to withdraw as a result of a juicy divorce scandal. Ah, family values! This left the party scrambling to find a new candidate on very short notice.

Interestingly, Dr. Andrea Barthwell has resigned from her position as assistant to Drug Czar John Walters, whom she has served since 2002 as the deputy director for demand reduction at the White House Office for National Drug Control Policy.

I have no idea whether she has any chance at all of getting the nomination. Perhaps neither does she, because, under federal law, she had to resign even to explore the possibility. One might wonder if this is just an exercise in resume padding, and/or getting out while the getting is good.

Frankly, I find myself with a very mixed reaction. In a moment I will explain why I think that Barthwell is completely unsuited for public office, but I think that her being a Senatorial candidate would make debating the Drug War, and especially the war on medical cannabis users, unavoidable.

Illinois State Sen. Kirk Dillard, who is member of the Republican State Central Committee, is quoted as saying, I've heard nothing but good things about her.

Well, Senator, what would you think about someone who lies to the American people to justify making war, not on a foreign dictator, but on sick and dying Americans?

That is what should be the central issue in a Barthwell senatorial campaign.

First, let us look at Barthwell's record.

She is a medical doctor, and, until her confirmation in 2002, was the president of the Board of Directors of the American Society of Addiction Medicine and a board member of the American Methadone Treatment Association.
See
UK Addiction Specialist Says, " Cannabis shouldn't be denied to deserving cases just because of the USA's ineffective worldwide " war on drugs " during the last 80 years. "

She had also been President of the Encounter Medical Group in Oak Park, Illinois and as President and Executive Vice President of two major drug treatment providers in Chicago, the BRASS Foundation and the Human Resources Development Institute. Previously, Dr. Barthwell served two terms as President of the Illinois Society of Addiction Medicine.
See
Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldn't Make This Up, But They Did.

However, this is not the part of her career that I find most disturbing. I think that her own words, in support of continuing the federal war on sick and dying Americans who want to use medical cannabis, demonstrate that she is not only unsuited to hold public office but also unsuited to practice medicine.

Most inexcusably, Dr. Barthwell has lied about the 1999 Institute of Medicine report on Medical Marijuana.

In an Op-ed, which is posted on the Drug Czar's website, Dr. Barthwell says, Simply put, there is no scientific evidence that qualifies smoked marijuana to be called medicine. Further, there is no support in the medical literature that marijuana, or indeed any medicine, should be smoked as the preferred form of administration. The harms to health are simply too great.

Marijuana advocates often cite the 1999 National Academy of Science's Institute of Medicine report as justifying the drug's medical use. But, in fact, the verdict of that report was " marijuana is not a modern medicine. " The institute was particularly troubled by the notion that crude marijuana might be smoked by patients, which it termed a harmful drug-delivery system.

In fact, the IOM report said, Until a non-smoked, rapid-onset cannabinoid drug delivery system becomes available, we acknowledge that there is no clear alternative for people suffering from chronic conditions that might be relieved by smoking marijuana, such as pain or AIDS wasting.

As that statement indicates, it is true that the IOM report was concerned about the risks of smoking, but five years later, a medical doctor who claims any knowledge of the subject must know that cannabis need not be smoked.

Moreover, no one claims that smoking is the preferred form of administration. She habitually misrepresents the views of those with whom she disagrees.

Although thesupposeddangers smoking cannabis have been greatly exaggerated, they are of dubious relevance for patients who are dying, or whose use would be intermittent. In any case, there are other means of administration, eating, drinking as a tea, and, of course, vaporization.
See
No Medicine Is Smoked. Okay, But Why Isn't Cannabis Sold Over-the-Counter? New MAPS/NORML Vaporizer Study Undermines Key Part Of Prohibitionist Party Line On Smoked-Marijuana.

In a press release, Marijuana as medicine? dated October 10, 2003, which was sent to the New England Governors' Summit on Drug Use, Dr. Barthwell, wrote, The hoax of using a smoked weed as medicine is the Trojan Horse of the new millennium. The claim that marijuana can be used as medicine is proving to be one of the worst scams drug legalizers have perpetrated on the American people.

In reality, smoked marijuana is far too complex, unstable, and harmful a substance to be approved as a medicine. In every instance claimed by legalizers as a use for smoked marijuana, there exist far better, legitimate, scientifically approved medications. Any argument supporting a smoked material as a medicine is dubious -- ridiculous even! The purpose of proposals to use marijuana as medicine is simple: make marijuana and other illicit substances more available to individuals and communities in our country.

There are three substantive points here.

First, she again ignores the IOM report that said, there is no clear alternative for people suffering from chronic conditions that might be relieved by smoking marijuana, such as pain or AIDS wasting.

Second, even the manufacturers of the better, legitimate, scientifically approved medications do not claim that they always work. If she does not know this, then she should not be practicing medicine.
See
New York Times Runs Pro-Medical Marijuana Op-ed By National Review Senior Editor Richard Brookhiser

Moreover, there are serious problems in the treatment of pain, especially, neuropathic pain. This is another fact that she should known, especially as an addiction specialist.
See
 " 50 percent of patients who died in hospitals suffered moderate to severe pain. " But We Are Told That There Is No Need For Medical Marijuana -- 2 Articles
and
Scottish MS Patient Says She Will Kill Herself When Trial Is Over. But GW Pharmaceutical's Research Proves That Her Death Will Really Be Murder. The Need for A Patients Rights Organization.
and
What Is More Important, Prohibition Or The Patients? The Death of Cheryl Miller Should Remind Us All To Demand A Change In Priorities. Should Pain Be A Crime?

Third, notice her attacks on the motives on medical cannabis advocates:
The hoax of using a smoked weed as medicine is the Trojan Horse of the new millennium. The claim that marijuana can be used as medicine is proving to be one of the worst scams drug legalizers have perpetrated on the American people.
See
Reading Between The Lies. New Version of An Old Lie About My Saying Medical Cannabis Is A Scam May Be Clue to New Prohibitionist Party Line. Only A Few Hundred Patients?

The purpose of proposals to use marijuana as medicine is simple: make marijuana and other illicit substances more available to individuals and communities in our country.

This is the antithesis of a scientific argument, and as a person who has a degree in psychology, she should be called upon to explain the basis of such a claim. On what does she base her expertise on the motives of her opponents?

The absurdity of this libel against advocates of medical cannabis is best understood when one looks at who is included in this scam. In addition to conservative laypersons like Richard Brookhiser, whose op-ed is linked above, even the editor of the New England Journal of Medicine has supported medical cannabis.

For an insight into his arguments and the prohibitionist opposition to medical cannabis see
Nahas versus Kassirer -- Fraud on Wall Street: How The Wall Street Journal defrauded the readers of its editorial page

Finally, prohibitionists like Dr. Barthwell like to claim that the support of medical cannabis is somehow an attack on modern medicine. But public support for medical cannabis about 75% is not based on any opinion on cannabis as medicine, even though many people actually know someone who has benefited from it. Rather, it is based on the public's opposition to the use of the criminal law against sick and dying people. And that is what this is really all about.
See
Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure.

Until very recently, I was not aware that Dr. Barthwell is an African American, but that fact certainly adds to the outrageousness of her position. I would love to hear her debate talk-show host Montel Williams, who has multiple sclerosis.

Dr. Barthwell, what would be the appropriate prison sentence for Williams? Who duped him into supporting medical cannabis when you say that he does not need it?

But while prominent African Americans like Montel Williams are often able to take care of themselves, the same certainly cannot be said of poor blacks in America or Britain, or especially Africa.
See
Prohibition and The Prison State. Protecting Youth and Minorities. In DEAland, The UK and France Prisons Are Full.

In fact, the suppression of medical cannabis has an even more devastating effect in Africa and other impoverished areas of the world where AIDS is rampant and conventional medicines are unaffordable even if they were available.
See
America Sentenced to Life In Prison For Marijuana. Really! Another One We Couldn't Make Up. And As Usual, It Is Even Worse for Others. DEAland's War On Cannabis Disastrous for Poor Countries.
and links

Remember, Barthwell is a medical doctor and she knows that the Hippocratic oath begins with the admonition, First, do no harm. Consequently, I think that given Dr. Barthwell's public record, she is not only unsuited for public office, but she should not be practicing medicine.

In any case, it seems unlikely that she will get the Illinois Republican Senatorial nomination, but not because the Republican leadership will object to her lies in the service of the Drug War. But at a time when the country is debating whether lies and incompetence led us into a foreign war, we really need to be asking the same question about the Drug War and especially the war on the sick and dying.
See
Is the War On Drugs A Just War. "? Should It Be Easier To Justify Violence Against A Foreign Dictatorship Than Against Peaceful Citizens Of One's Own Country?
